items.title: Metropolis acceptance in the perturbation chain
items.spec: In the perturbation phase, keep the current packing as the chain state instead of always returning to the global best. After each perturbation and SLSQP polish with repair, accept the candidate if its radius sum is higher, or with probability exp((new_sum - cur_sum) / T) otherwise. Set T to 0.003 at the start of the phase and decay it geometrically to 1e-5 by the time limit. Always record the global best separately and return it. Use rng for all draws.

items.title: 1/5-rule adaptive perturbation step size
items.spec: In the perturbation phase, maintain a noise scale sigma starting at 0.02 for the Gaussian shake of the chosen circles. Count successes (candidate beats the current chain state). Every 10 perturbations, multiply sigma by 1.2 if the success rate over that window exceeded 0.2, otherwise multiply by 0.83, and clip sigma to [0.003, 0.08]. Keep the existing move types and the existing SLSQP polish; only the step size becomes adaptive.

items.title: Stall-triggered switch from restarts to perturbation
items.spec: Replace the fixed 30 percent switch point with a stall rule. Keep running random restarts, and track how many consecutive restarts fail to improve the best radius sum. Once that count reaches 8, or 60 percent of the budget has been used, switch to the perturbation search from the best packing. The minimum restart phase is 10 percent of the budget. Everything else stays the same.

items.title: Cut-and-splice crossover of elite packings
items.spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings found by restarts. For a fraction of the perturbation steps, choose two elites at random. Draw a random line through the unit square, take the circles of the first parent on one side and the circles of the second parent on the other side, and fix the total count at n by dropping or adding the smallest-radius circles, with new circles placed at random. Run the existing SLSQP polish with a short iteration cap on the child, then repair. Accept the child into the elite set if it beats the worst elite and is not a duplicate.

items.title: Squared-radius reparametrisation
items.spec: Change the SLSQP variables so that each radius is r = s^2, with s as the optimised variable and bounds on s of [0, 0.5]. Constraints become (distance squared compared to (s_i + s_j)^2) or equivalently keep the existing distance constraint with r replaced by s*s. Map the result back to radii before repair. The constraint remains smooth at zero radius, and this removes the active bound on radii. Keep all other settings and the restart logic unchanged.

items.title: Latin-hypercube starting centres
items.spec: For fresh random starts in _solve_once, draw the centre coordinates from a Latin hypercube over [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW] instead of i.i.d. uniform. Use n strata per axis, shuffle each axis independently with rng.permutation, and place one sample in each stratum with a uniform offset inside it. Keep the radius initialisation and the warm-start branch unchanged, so the only change is how the starting centres are spread.

items.title: Scale-recovery bisection after repair
items.spec: After _repair, the radii are often shrunk more than needed. Add a final step: find the largest factor f in [1, 1.05] such that the radii multiplied by f still give a valid packing, using bisection with 30 steps. Validity means every circle is inside the square and every pair satisfies d >= r_i + r_j, computed exactly. Apply the largest valid f, then subtract SHRINK as before. Only accept the scaled radii if the check passes, so the output stays valid.

items.title: Random per-restart iteration budget
items.spec: Give each random restart its own SLSQP iteration cap, drawn log-uniformly from [40, 400] using rng. Short caps let many starts be screened cheaply, and long caps let good starts converge. Keep the existing best-so-far update rule. Do not change the perturbation phase, which keeps MAX_ITER.

items.title: Two independent perturbation chains
items.spec: In the perturbation phase, run two independent chains from the best restart packing, each with its own rng stream derived from seed (for example seed+1 and seed+2). Each chain uses the existing shake-and-polish move. Split the remaining time evenly between chains by alternating one step at a time, and return the best packing across both chains. This adds diversity to the local search without changing the moves.

items.title: Rattler reinsertion into the largest hole
items.spec: In the perturbation phase, identify rattlers in the current best packing: circles with fewer than 2 contacts, where a contact means the gap between two circles or between a circle and a wall is below 1e-6. With probability 1/2 per perturbation, remove one rattler chosen at random and reinsert it at the point with the largest clearance, found by checking 2000 random candidates against all circles and walls. Set its radius to that clearance, then run the existing SLSQP polish and repair. If there are no rattlers, use the smallest circle instead.

items.title: Maximin starts plus 30% restart share base
items.spec: Make half of fresh random starts use farthest-point (maximin) sampled centres: for each start, pick each new centre as the best of 400 random candidates in [0.03,0.97]^2 maximising the minimum distance to already chosen centres, with initial radii 0.05. Keep the 30% restart then perturbation structure unchanged. This is the slot 34 idea with a replicate-ready clean implementation.

items.title: Maximin starts with shake-all perturbation
items.spec: Combine two replicated winners. Fresh starts: half use maximin centres (best of 400 candidates). Perturbation phase: replace the 2-3 circle move with shaking all centres by normal noise sd 0.05, running SLSQP with maxiter=60 from there, then continuing the usual maxiter to convergence only if the 60-iteration result is within 0.01 of the best sum. Accept if the repaired sum improves.

items.title: Maximin starts, 20% restart share, shake perturbation
items.spec: Use maximin starts for half of fresh restarts, shift the restart share from 30% to 20% of the budget, and in the perturbation phase use a mix: 50% shake-all centres with sd drawn uniformly from [0.03,0.07] followed by SLSQP, 50% the existing move of 2-3 circles. Accept if better.

items.title: Maximin starts with perimeter ring
items.spec: For half of fresh starts use maximin centres, and for the other half place 12 circles in a jittered perimeter ring (distance 0.03-0.08 from the walls, evenly spaced along the boundary with jitter) and the remaining 14 at random in [0.2,0.8]^2. Initial radii 0.05. Keep the rest unchanged.

items.title: Two-stage SLSQP with maximin starts
items.spec: Run SLSQP in two stages for each fresh start: 40 iterations first, then 160 more from the result, with centres from maximin sampling (best of 400 candidates). Slots 15 and 34 each looked helpful on their own. Perturbation phase unchanged.

items.title: Scale constraints for SLSQP
items.spec: Multiply pair-distance constraints by 1.0 and the wall and radius-positivity constraints by 1.0, but divide the objective by n (use -mean radius times 10) so SLSQP's line search is better conditioned. Equivalently scale the objective to -sum(r)/n*10. Nothing else changes. Check that the repair step still gives valid packings.

items.title: Smaller SHRINK with verified repair
items.spec: Lower SHRINK from 1e-9 to 2e-11. After repair, verify exactly in double precision: all pair distances >= r_i+r_j and walls hold with c-r>=0 and c+r<=1. If any check fails, subtract 1e-10 from all radii and retest, up to 5 times. The harness tolerance is 1e-10, so the gain is small but free.

items.title: Radius-growth maximin start
items.spec: For half of fresh starts, choose maximin centres (best of 400 candidates), then set initial radii by greedy growth: r_i = min(wall distance, half of the distance to the nearest other centre) * 0.9. SLSQP then starts from a nearly feasible, varied-radius configuration.

items.title: Hex-row starts with random row counts
items.spec: Half of fresh starts use staggered rows: choose a row count k from {5,6} and per-row counts that sum to 26 with entries 4-6, placed evenly in y and x with a half-spacing offset on alternate rows, plus gaussian jitter sd 0.03, initial radius 0.06. The other half use maximin starts. Perturbation phase unchanged.

items.title: Large-neighbourhood window re-solve
items.spec: In the perturbation phase, for a third of moves choose a random point in the square, take the 6 circles nearest to it, re-randomise their centres uniformly within a disc of radius 0.2 around the point, set their radii to 0.03, and run SLSQP on all circles with maxiter 100. Accept if the repaired sum improves. Other moves stay the same.

items.title: Re-run maximin starts (slot 34) as the new base
items.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 (rng.random()<0.5) replace the uniform initial centres with farthest-point (maximin) centres. Draw 400 candidate points with rng.uniform(INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW, (400,2)). Pick the first point at random with rng.integers. Then n-1 times, add the candidate whose minimum distance to the points already chosen is largest (keep a running min-distance array and update it with np.minimum after each pick). Radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Change nothing else. This reproduces slot 34, which scored -2.6342/-2.6337 over 2 runs against the incumbent's -2.6313, so it should be confirmed and adopted.

items.title: Maximin starts plus shake-all perturbation
items.spec: Add the slot-34 maximin start: in _solve_once with start None and rng.random()<0.5, take 400 candidates from rng.uniform(INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW, (400,2)), choose a random first one, then greedily add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set until there are n. In the perturbation branch (start not None), add a third move with probability 1/3: c0 = clip(c0 + rng.normal(0, 0.05, c0.shape), 0.01, 0.99), keep r0, and run SLSQP with maxiter 60 instead of MAX_ITER (pass maxiter as an argument to _solve_once). The other two thirds keep the current 50/50 relocate/jitter moves at full MAX_ITER. Repair and the accept-if-better logic stay the same.

items.title: Maximin starts with restart share 15%
items.spec: Add maximin starts for half of the fresh starts: when start is None and rng.random()<0.5, draw 400 candidates uniform in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, pick a random first candidate, then repeatedly add the candidate that maximizes the minimum distance to the chosen points until there are n centres. Radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Also, in solve, change the switch to the perturbation phase from 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit to 0.15*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit. Nothing else changes.

items.title: Maximin starts with radius-growth initial radii
items.spec: For fresh starts (start None), always use maximin centres: take 400 candidates from rng.uniform(0.05, 0.95, (400,2)), pick a random first candidate, then greedily add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen points until there are n. Set each initial radius to min(0.5 * distance to its nearest other centre, distance to the nearest wall) * 0.9, so the start is almost feasible and the circles already have different sizes. Feed that to SLSQP as x0. The perturbation phase is unchanged.

items.title: Maximin starts plus perimeter-ring starts mix
items.spec: Split fresh starts (start None) into three types, chosen with rng.random(): with probability 0.4 use maximin centres (400 candidates uniform in [0.1,0.9]^2, random first pick, then greedily add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set); with probability 0.3 put 12 circles in a jittered perimeter ring (parameter t uniform around the square boundary, at distance uniform(0.03,0.12) inward from the wall) and the other 14 uniform in [0.2,0.8]^2; otherwise use the current uniform start. All radii start at INIT_RADIUS. The perturbation phase is unchanged.

items.title: Early abort of weak restarts with maximin starts
items.spec: Add maximin starts for half of the fresh starts (400 candidates uniform in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, random first pick, then greedily add the candidate with the largest min-distance to the chosen points). In the fresh-start phase only, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 uses maxiter=40. Repair a copy of the stage-1 result; if its radii sum is below best_sum - 0.03, return the repaired stage-1 result without continuing. Otherwise continue SLSQP from the stage-1 x for 160 more iterations. To do this, give _solve_once a threshold argument (None in the perturbation phase) and keep the final repair in solve as it is.

items.title: Large-neighbourhood re-solve of a spatial window
items.spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 1/3, use a window move instead of the current moves. Pick a random point p uniform in [0.15,0.85]^2. Take the k=5 to 7 circles whose centres are nearest to p, put them at new positions p + rng.uniform(-0.15,0.15,(k,2)) clipped to [0.02,0.98], and set their radii to 0.02. Keep all other circles as they are in the best packing. Then run the full SLSQP from this x0 with MAX_ITER. The other two thirds keep the current 50/50 relocate-2-3/jitter moves. Accept only if better, as now.

items.title: Annealed acceptance in the perturbation phase
items.spec: In solve, during the perturbation phase, keep a 'current' packing separate from 'best'. Perturb the current packing, not the best one. Accept the new packing as current if its sum is above current_sum - T, where T decays linearly from 0.004 at the start of the perturbation phase to 0 at the end of the time budget; always update best when a new sum exceeds best_sum. If 15 perturbations in a row fail to improve best, reset current to best. Everything else, including the moves themselves, stays the same.

items.title: Final SLSQP polish with tight tolerance before repair
items.spec: Keep the search as it is. Stop the loop at 0.75*time_limit instead of TIME_FRACTION. Then take the best packing (its unrepaired centres and radii) and run one SLSQP from it with options {'maxiter': 1000, 'ftol': 1e-13}. Repair the result with _repair and return it only if its sum beats the stored best. Also store the unrepaired SLSQP output next to the best repaired packing, so that the polish starts from the raw optimum and not from the shrunk radii. Guard the polish so that it starts only if at least 4 s of CPU time remain.

items.title: Constraint scaling for SLSQP
items.spec: In cons inside _solve_once, scale the pairwise constraint by dividing d by (r_i + r_j + 0.05). This keeps its sign and makes its magnitude comparable across pairs. Multiply the wall and radius-nonnegativity constraints by 10 so that they are of similar scale to the pair terms. Scaling an inequality by a positive factor does not change the feasible set, but it changes how SLSQP weights the constraints and can help it converge to better local optima. Repair stays the same. Change nothing else.

items.title: Maximin starts plus shake-all perturbation move
items.spec: Combine the two replicated winners (slot 34 and slot 31). (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 build the initial centres by farthest-point sampling instead of uniform: draw 400 candidate points uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, pick the first at random, then repeatedly add the candidate whose minimum distance to the already chosen points is largest, until n are chosen; radii stay INIT_RADIUS. (2) In the perturbation phase (start is not None) add a third move with probability 1/3: add normal noise of sd 0.05 to ALL centres (clip to [0.01, 0.99]), run SLSQP with maxiter 60, and only if the resulting radius sum is within 0.02 of the best sum continue from that point with another 140 iterations; otherwise return the 60-iteration result. The other two moves (relocate 2-3 circles, jitter sd 0.02) share the remaining 2/3 equally. Keep everything else, including _repair and the 30% restart share.

items.title: Maximin starts mixed with perimeter-ring starts
items.spec: Change only how fresh random starts (start is None in _solve_once) pick centres; draw the start type uniformly from three options. (a) Uniform as now. (b) Maximin: draw 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and pick n by farthest-point sampling (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (c) Ring plus maximin interior: place 12 circles on the perimeter, 3 per wall at evenly spaced positions along the wall with jitter of sd 0.03, at distance uniform(0.03, 0.12) from that wall, then pick the other 14 centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 candidates in [0.2, 0.8]^2, where the distance is measured to all chosen points including the ring. Initial radii stay INIT_RADIUS. Leave the perturbation phase and repair unchanged.

items.title: Full combination: maximin, ring and shake-all
items.spec: Implement three changes together. (1) Fresh starts: with probability 0.5 use farthest-point sampling (400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, first point random, then repeatedly add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen points) for all n centres. (2) With probability 0.25 use 12 perimeter circles (3 per wall, evenly spaced with sd 0.03 jitter, distance uniform(0.03, 0.12) from the wall) plus 14 interior centres drawn uniformly in [0.2, 0.8]^2; the remaining 0.25 stay uniform as now. (3) In the perturbation phase, one third of the moves add normal noise of sd 0.05 to all centres (clip to [0.01, 0.99]) and run SLSQP at the normal MAX_ITER; the other two moves split the rest equally. Keep the 30% restart share, _repair and all constants.

items.title: Maximin for every fresh start, with varied candidate count
items.spec: Slot 34 used maximin centres for half of the fresh starts; test using them for all. In _solve_once, when start is None, always build centres by farthest-point sampling: draw m uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, where m is drawn per start from {60, 150, 400} (fewer candidates gives a more irregular layout, more gives a near-uniform one), choose the first point at random and then repeatedly add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set until n are chosen. Then add normal jitter of sd 0.01 to the centres. Initial radii stay INIT_RADIUS. Nothing else changes.

items.title: Maximin starts with a 20% restart share
items.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to those already chosen) instead of uniform draws. (2) In solve, replace the hard-coded 0.3 with a new constant RESTART_SHARE = 0.2, so perturbation of the best packing starts after 20% of the usable time instead of 30%. The idea is that better starts need fewer restarts to find a good basin, leaving more time to refine it.

items.title: Maximin starts with feasible nearest-neighbour radii
items.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [0.05, 0.95]^2 (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen points). For these starts set each initial radius to 0.48 times the distance to the nearest other centre, capped by the distance to the nearest wall, instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS, so SLSQP starts from a feasible and already fairly dense packing with unequal radii. The other half of the fresh starts and the whole perturbation phase stay as they are.

items.title: Maximin starts with mirror-symmetric variant
items.spec: Change only fresh starts (start is None in _solve_once), with three equally likely types. (a) Uniform as now. (b) Maximin: farthest-point sampling of n centres from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (c) Symmetric maximin: farthest-point sample 13 centres from 200 candidates in [INIT_LOW, 0.47] x [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], mirror them through x = 0.5 to get the other 13, then add normal jitter of sd 0.005 to all centres to break exact symmetry. Initial radii stay INIT_RADIUS. Leave the perturbation phase untouched.

items.title: Maximin starts and shorter SLSQP runs in the perturbation phase
items.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (2) Add a constant PERTURB_ITER = 100 and use it as SLSQP maxiter when start is not None (MAX_ITER = 200 stays for fresh starts). A perturbed copy of a good packing is close to a local optimum, so shorter runs should allow about twice as many perturbation trials in the same time.

items.title: Maximin starts and near-pair constraints in the perturbation phase
items.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (2) When start is not None, make SLSQP cheaper by restricting the pair constraints: after building the perturbed x0, keep only pairs (i, j) whose centre distance in x0 is below 0.45, and keep all pairs involving any relocated circle (the idx circles). Build iu from this subset. Wall and radius constraints stay complete. _repair already checks all pairs, so a dropped pair that ends up overlapping is still fixed before the result is compared. This should cut the constraint count by more than half and allow more perturbation trials.

items.title: Maximin starts with analytic Jacobian for more trials
items.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (2) Pass exact derivatives to SLSQP: jac of the objective is zeros for the 2n centre entries and -1 for the n radius entries; the constraint Jacobian is a dense (m, 3n) array built with vectorised index assignment: for pair k = (i, j), the derivative with respect to c_i is (c_i - c_j)/dist, with respect to c_j the negative, and -1 for r_i and r_j (guard dist with max(dist, 1e-12)); the wall rows are +1 or -1 on the centre coordinate and -1 on the radius; the last n rows are +1 on the radius. Analytic gradients alone were neutral in the pure-restart script (slot 3); here the test is whether the extra speed gives more perturbation trials on top of better starts.
